newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy expects fall in rates from budget - unions.
newsitem.headline: Italy expects fall in rates from budget - unions.

text.p: The government expects its 1997 budget, which it will formally unveil later on Friday, to trigger a sharp fall in interest rates, union leaders said after meeting Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Union officials added the government would also follow France's example of using proceeds from state companies to cut its deficit, so long as the French plan gets the backing of the European Commission.
The French government proposed a one-off payment of 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom to cut the central state deficit.

EU commissioner for Economic and Financial Affairs Yves-Thibault de Silguy has said the French budget probably conformed with Maastricht treaty provisions governing deficits, but would be examined on its technical merits by the Commission.

Union leaders said earlier that the 1997 budget would look to cut between 37 to 38 trillion lire off next year's deficit. In addition there will be a one-off "Euro-tax" which could raise up to 13 to 15 trillion lire in 1997.

Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said last weekend that a rigourous budget was needed before any further monetary easing. The government is anxious for a rate cut to reduce the enormous interest bill it has to pay on its debt mountain.

Prodi is battling on all fronts to cut Italy's deficit to gross domestic product ratio to three per cent in 1997 from a forecast 6.09 percent this year, in a bid to push Italy into the first group of countries forming the single European currency.
As part of this policy, the government said it wanted to use proceeds from the planned privatisations of energy group Eni and electricity firm Enel to help cut the deficit.
A second tranche of Eni is due to be floated in October while the Enel sale is slated for early 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
